title: Graph visualization and editing
summary: Render, edit and interact with graph data in a web application. Compare maintained graph-editor libraries, feature fit, licensing and migration paths. The existing application currently uses AntV X6; the same evaluation applies to new graph-editor projects.
constraints: Must run within the target application's browser and runtime baseline; record the exact baseline before judging compatibility
Preserve existing graph editing, selection, transform, history and export behaviour during any upgrade or migration
Permissive license across the full dependency tree
No unfixed high or critical advisories
No install scripts in the dependency tree
Do not mix X6 major lines: v3 core must use its bundled plugins, and 2.x plugins must not be installed with v3
If the application runtime includes Node or SSR, verify native ESM/CJS loading before adopting X6 v3
If npm provenance is unavailable, pin exact versions and record the gap
out_of_scope: Backend graph database and query language
Rewriting the application or choosing a new UI framework
Detailed benchmark against every graph library
notes: The requirement covers two distinct X6 lines. v2: @antv/x6@2.19.2 plus @antv/x6-common, @antv/x6-geometry and the separate 2.x plugins; this is the stack for existing X6 applications, but the v2 line was marked deprecated at 2.19.0 and is not a long-term option. v3: @antv/x6@3.1.8 bundles common, geometry and the official plugins; it requires Node >=20, changes panning, animation and scroller behaviour, and its npm package currently fails native Node ESM and CJS loading (see docs/x6-v2-v3-audit.md). React nodes use the official @antv/x6-react-shape 3.0.1 package, which peers React >=18 and is browser-only; it was validated in a React 19.2.0 spike on 2026-11-04. Do not install the deprecated 3.0.0 plugin packages or mix v3 core with 2.x plugins. D3 is the named alternative, but it does not provide X6's editing/plugin layer. The consuming application team must record its actual lockfile, browser baseline and plugin usage before any migration verdict; this board has no access to that application. Choosing v2 is a time-boxed bridge, not a final destination; its 12-month maintenance window closes on 2026-11-17, so the consuming application must remove it by that date or record a new time-boxed exception.
